chapters.heading: UNITED STATES CAPITOL POLICE REFORM AND ACCOUNTABILITY

sections.heading: Deployment outside the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds
paragraphs: (a) The Capitol Police may provide protective services for Members of Congress, officers of Congress, congressional employees, witnesses, invited guests, visitors, and other persons whose safety is connected to the conduct of official congressional business.

(b) The Speaker of the House of Representatives, the President pro tempore of the Senate, the Majority Leader of the House of Representatives, and the Majority Leader of the Senate shall be eligible for continuing protective services by virtue of their offices. Such protective services may be maintained without a separate threat finding, Board vote, emergency determination, or temporary authorization.

(c) The Board may designate additional congressional leadership offices, officers of Congress, committee chairs, ranking members, or other persons whose duties create recurring security concerns as eligible for continuing protective services.

(d) Continuing protective services for chamber leadership may include physical security, escorts, secure transportation, threat assessment, site security, event security, access control, emergency response, travel security, coordination with other lawful security agencies, and any other protective measure reasonably necessary to protect the person or preserve the performance of official duties.

(e) Protective services may be provided where a person is present within the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, attending or participating in a congressional proceeding, traveling for official congressional business, appearing before either House or a committee, assisting a congressional investigation, attending an official event, or otherwise exposed to a threat because of duties, testimony, employment, invitation, public visibility, or association with Congress.

(f) The Chief may authorize temporary protective services without prior approval of the Board where an immediate threat exists, where delay would endanger the person to be protected, where protection is necessary to secure an ongoing congressional proceeding, or where the person’s official duties create a temporary security concern.

(g) Temporary protective services authorized by the Chief shall be limited to the time and measures reasonably necessary to address the threat, official function, travel, emergency, or security concern that justified the protection.

(h) The Capitol Police may protect a witness or invited guest before, during, and after a congressional proceeding where the person’s safety, access, testimony, cooperation, or ability to participate in congressional business may be threatened, obstructed, intimidated, or disrupted.

(i) The Capitol Police may protect congressional employees and staff where threats or safety concerns arise from their official duties, employment in a congressional office, service to a committee, handling of sensitive information, public-facing responsibilities, or presence at a congressional proceeding or secured area.

(j) Protective services shall not be used to shield any person from lawful process, prevent congressional oversight, avoid questioning by either House or a committee, obstruct an investigation, interfere with a lawful arrest, or prevent the execution of any lawful order issued by Congress, either House, a committee, a court, or another lawful authority.

(k) The Chief shall maintain records of protective services provided under this section, including the person or category of person protected, the general basis for protection, the duration of protection, the type of protection provided, any outside agency involved, and any security incident connected to the protection.

(l) Records concerning protective services may be maintained in closed form where disclosure would endanger a protected person, reveal sensitive security procedures, compromise an active threat response, or expose private personal information, but such records shall remain available for lawful review by the Board.

sections.heading: Special officers of the Capitol Police
paragraphs: (a) During an emergency, major security event, major congressional proceeding, joint session, ceremonial event, threat response, temporary jurisdiction operation, protective assignment, or other circumstance requiring additional law enforcement personnel, the Chief may appoint special officers of the Capitol Police.

(b) The House Sergeant at Arms may request the appointment of special officers for the protection of House-controlled areas, House proceedings, Members of the House, officers of the House, House employees, House witnesses, invited guests of the House, or other persons or functions connected to the official business of the House.

(c) The Senate Sergeant at Arms may request the appointment of special officers for the protection of Senate-controlled areas, Senate proceedings, Senators, officers of the Senate, Senate employees, Senate witnesses, invited guests of the Senate, or other persons or functions connected to the official business of the Senate.

(d) Where immediate action is necessary to protect life, prevent serious injury, respond to violence, secure a chamber proceeding, protect a Member of Congress, or preserve the safety of a House-controlled or Senate-controlled area, the Sergeant at Arms of the affected House may temporarily designate qualified law enforcement personnel as special officers for that House’s controlled spaces or proceedings.

(e) A temporary designation made by a Sergeant at Arms shall be reported to the Chief as soon as practicable. Upon receiving notice, the Chief shall confirm, limit, coordinate, or terminate the designation as necessary to preserve unified command, comply with this Act, and protect the affected House.

(f) A special officer may be appointed or designated from among law enforcement officers of the United States, a State, a local government, or any other lawful law enforcement agency made available by the employing authority.

(g) A member of the uniformed services, including a member of the National Guard, may be appointed or designated as a special officer when made available by the proper military or governmental authority.

(h) A special officer shall exercise only the authority granted by the Chief or the relevant Sergeant at Arms and only within the authority of the Capitol Police, the affected House, or the appointing authority under this Act.

(i) A special officer appointed by the Chief may assist in policing the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, securing congressional proceedings, providing protective services, controlling access, responding to emergencies, assisting with removals or arrests, protecting persons or property, or carrying out another specific duty assigned by the Chief.

(j) A special officer temporarily designated by a Sergeant at Arms may assist in securing that House’s controlled spaces, protecting that House’s proceedings, enforcing lawful access rules, protecting Members and officers of that House, escorting witnesses or guests, removing disorderly persons, responding to emergencies, and carrying out lawful security directions of the relevant House.

(k) An appointment or designation as a special officer shall be temporary and shall last only for the period, event, emergency, assignment, proceeding, or operation specified at the time of appointment or designation.

(l) The Chief or the relevant Sergeant at Arms may revoke, suspend, limit, or modify the authority of a special officer appointed or designated by that officer at any time. (m)A special officer shall remain subject to the command of the Chief when performing duties for the Capitol Police generally, and shall remain subject to the relevant Sergeant at Arms when assigned to the controlled spaces or proceedings of that House. Where an assignment involves both Capitol Police operations and the controlled spaces of either House, the Chief and relevant Sergeant at Arms shall coordinate command and duties.
(n) A special officer shall not become an employee of the Capitol Police or either House solely by reason of appointment or designation as a special officer.
(o) A special officer shall not receive pay from the Capitol Police or either House for service as a special officer unless otherwise authorized by law, agreement, rule, or appropriation.

(p) The Capitol Police, the House Sergeant at Arms, and the Senate Sergeant at Arms may enter into reimbursement agreements or support agreements with any federal, State, local, military, or other lawful authority that provides personnel serving as special officers under this section.

(q) The Chief and the Sergeants at Arms shall ensure, where practicable, that each special officer receives instructions concerning the scope of authority, chain of command, use of force, arrest authority, access rules, political neutrality, protection of congressional proceedings, and limits applicable under this Act before performing duties as a special officer.

(r) The Chief and the relevant Sergeant at Arms shall maintain records of special officer appointments and designations, including the identifying information of the officer, the employing authority, the reason for appointment or designation, the scope of authority granted, the duration of service, the assignment performed, and any arrest, detention, removal, use of force, injury, complaint, or major incident involving the special officer.

(s) The Chief shall report special officer appointments to the Board as soon as practicable where the appointment involves an emergency, a major security event, a joint session, a deployment outside the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, uniformed services personnel, or more than a limited number of outside officers.

(t) A Sergeant at Arms shall report temporary special officer designations to the Board as soon as practicable where the designation involves an emergency, chamber security, a major proceeding, uniformed services personnel, use of force, arrest, detention, or a substantial security incident.

(u) The Board may limit, suspend, or terminate the use of special officers where necessary to protect Congress, preserve accountability, prevent misuse, maintain unified command, or ensure compliance with this Act.
